expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides types.ts, selection.ts, api.ts, useBulkAction.ts, ConfirmDeleteDialog.tsx, BulkActionsBar.tsx, DocumentsTable.tsx, and Pagination component with full implementations.

expectations.text: Produces actual working component code rather than only a list of recommendations
expectations.evidence: All components written with complete JSX, event handlers, Tailwind styling, and state management including reducer pattern and hooks.

expectations.text: Makes the destructive action recoverable rather than relying on a confirmation dialog alone
expectations.evidence: Soft-deletes with 30-day trash period; provides undoToken in BulkResult; toast offers 'Undo' action: 'toast.success(label, { duration: 10_000, action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => undoBulk(result.undoToken!) }'

expectations.text: Shows the count of affected items before the action is taken
expectations.evidence: BulkActionsBar displays '{count.toLocaleString()} document{count === 1 ? '' : 's'} selected' before any button interaction.

expectations.text: Distinguishes select-all-on-page from select-all-matching rather than conflating them
expectations.evidence: Selection has include vs allMatching modes; table includes explicit escalation banners showing difference; bar shows '(all matching your filters)' only when mode is allMatching.

expectations.text: Separates the destructive action from the benign one visually or spatially
expectations.evidence: Archive button with slate-300 border, followed by '<div className="mx-1 h-6 w-px bg-slate-200" aria-hidden="true" />', then Delete with red-200 border and red-700 text.

expectations.text: Does not make the destructive action the default focus or primary button
expectations.evidence: Delete button styled identically to Archive (white bg, borders only); dialog focuses input or cancel: '(mustType ? inputRef : cancelRef).current?.focus()' — never the delete button.

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: Explicit 'Server contract you need to hold up' section: '**Re-apply the tenant/permission scope to `filter` server-side.** The client sends a filter, not a list — never trust it as an authorization boundary.'

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Closes with 'What this shape makes impossible, and what it leaves open': lists Rung 1 impossibilities (sending 50 IDs, stale filter, double-apply, silent growth); Rung 2 choices; Left possible on purpose.
